+package chi
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// CORSOptions configures the CORS middleware and Mux.EnableCORSWithOptions.
+type CORSOptions struct {
+	// AllowOrigin is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The wildcard
+	// "*" allows any origin; an empty string sends no header, so no
+	// cross-origin caller is allowed.
+	AllowOrigin string
+
+	// AllowMethods lists the methods named in Access-Control-Allow-Methods on
+	// a preflight response. When empty, the methods the requested route
+	// answers are detected from the router.
+	AllowMethods []string
+
+	// AllowHeaders lists the request headers named in
+	// Access-Control-Allow-Headers on a preflight response. When empty, the
+	// headers the browser asked for are allowed.
+	AllowHeaders []string
+
+	// ExposeHeaders lists the response headers a browser may read, sent as
+	// Access-Control-Expose-Headers.
+	ExposeHeaders []string
+
+	// MaxAge is how many seconds a browser may cache a preflight response,
+	// sent as Access-Control-Max-Age. Zero sends no header.
+	MaxAge int
+
+	// AllowCredentials sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true, which
+	// lets the browser send cookies and authorization headers.
+	AllowCredentials bool
+}
+
+// DefaultCORSOptions returns options that allow any origin, the common request
+// headers and a one hour preflight cache. The allowed methods are left empty,
+// so they are detected from the routes.
+func DefaultCORSOptions() CORSOptions {
+	return CORSOptions{
+		AllowOrigin:  "*",
+		AllowHeaders: []string{"Accept", "Authorization", "Content-Type", "X-CSRF-Token"},
+		MaxAge:       3600,
+	}
+}
+
+// CORS returns a middleware that adds the CORS headers of options to every
+// response and answers preflight requests itself.
+//
+// Every OPTIONS request counts as a preflight: it is answered with 204 and the
+// Access-Control-Allow-Methods, -Allow-Headers and -Max-Age headers, and never
+// reaches the route's own OPTIONS handler. A request for a path that no route
+// answers, with no AllowMethods set to advertise, is passed on to the next
+// handler, so the router still reports it as not found.
+//
+// The methods of a route are detected through the routing context, so the
+// middleware has to run inside a chi router.
+func CORS(options CORSOptions) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	policy := newCORSPolicy(options)
+	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+			policy.setHeaders(w.Header(), r)
+			if r.Method == http.MethodOptions && policy.preflight(w, r) {
+				return
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// corsPolicy is a CORSOptions with its header values joined once, when the
+// middleware is made, instead of on every request.
+type corsPolicy struct {
+	origin      string
+	methods     string
+	headers     string
+	expose      string
+	maxAge      string
+	credentials bool
+}
+
+func newCORSPolicy(options CORSOptions) *corsPolicy {
+	p := &corsPolicy{
+		origin:      options.AllowOrigin,
+		methods:     strings.Join(options.AllowMethods, ", "),
+		headers:     strings.Join(options.AllowHeaders, ", "),
+		expose:      strings.Join(options.ExposeHeaders, ", "),
+		credentials: options.AllowCredentials,
+	}
+	if options.MaxAge > 0 {
+		p.maxAge = strconv.Itoa(options.MaxAge)
+	}
+	return p
+}
+
+// setHeaders sets the headers every response carries, preflight or not.
+func (p *corsPolicy) setHeaders(h http.Header, r *http.Request) {
+	if origin := p.allowOrigin(r); origin != "" {
+		h.Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
+		if origin != "*" {
+			h.Add("Vary", "Origin")
+		}
+	}
+	if p.credentials {
+		h.Set("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true")
+	}
+	if p.expose != "" {
+		h.Set("Access-Control-Expose-Headers", p.expose)
+	}
+}
